title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
titleUz: Do‘st orttirish va odamlarga ta’sir o‘tkazish
author: Dale Carnegie
tagline: Samimiy e’tibor, aniq minnatdorlik va hurmatli kelishmovchilik orqali yaxshiroq suhbatlar quring.
intro: Sizni chindan tushunishgan suhbat qanday bo‘lgan edi? Bu darsda Deyl Karnegining boshqalarga qiziqish, samimiy minnatdorlik, tanqidsiz muloqot va xatoni tan olish haqidagi tamoyillarini maktab to‘garagi misolida o‘rganasiz.
learnPoints: Boshqalarga chin dildan qiziqish va tinglash
Xatoni tan olish va qadr-qimmatni saqlash
attribution: Independent Bookly summary and commentary on “How to Win Friends and Influence People” by Dale Carnegie. Original examples by Bookly. AI-narrated. Not endorsed by the author or publisher. Muallif yoki nashriyot tomonidan tasdiqlanmagan mustaqil Bookly sharhi; kitobning tanlangan g‘oyalarini tanishtiradi va to‘liq kitob o‘rnini bosmaydi.

sentences.en: Think about the last conversation that left you feeling understood.
sentences.uz: Sizni tushunishganini his qilgan oxirgi suhbatingizni eslang.

sentences.en: What did the other person do?
sentences.uz: Suhbatdoshingiz nima qildi?

sentences.en: Perhaps they asked a thoughtful question, remembered something important to you, or let you finish without interrupting.
sentences.uz: Balki u o‘ylab berilgan savol bergandir, siz uchun muhim narsani eslab qolgandir yoki gapingizni bo‘lmasdan oxirigacha tinglagandir.

sentences.en: Their attention may have mattered more than any impressive story they told.
sentences.uz: Uning e’tibori u aytib bergan har qanday ta’sirli hikoyadan ko‘ra muhimroq bo‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkin.

sentences.en: You're listening to Bookly's summary of How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie.
sentences.uz: Siz Deyl Karnegining «How to Win Friends and Influence People» («Do‘st orttirish va odamlarga ta’sir o‘tkazish») kitobi bo‘yicha Bookly qisqacha mazmunini tinglayapsiz.

sentences.en: Its central lesson is that relationships improve when you take other people's feelings, interests, and dignity seriously.
sentences.uz: Uning asosiy saboqi: boshqalarning his-tuyg‘ulari, qiziqishlari va qadr-qimmatiga jiddiy munosabatda bo‘lsangiz, munosabatlar yaxshilanadi.

sentences.en: Imagine you've joined a new school club.
sentences.uz: Maktabdagi yangi to‘garakka qo‘shilganingizni tasavvur qiling.

sentences.en: You want to make friends, so you spend the first meeting explaining your achievements.
sentences.uz: Siz do‘st orttirmoqchisiz, shuning uchun birinchi uchrashuvni o‘z yutuqlaringiz haqida gapirib o‘tkazasiz.

sentences.en: People listen politely, but the conversation goes flat.
sentences.uz: Odamlar xushmuomalalik bilan tinglashadi, ammo suhbat qovushmaydi.

sentences.en: At the next meeting, you ask another member how she made a design she's working on.
sentences.uz: Keyingi uchrashuvda boshqa bir a’zodan ustida ishlayotgan dizaynini qanday yaratganini so‘raysiz.

sentences.en: You listen, ask a follow-up question, and discover a shared interest.
sentences.uz: Tinglaysiz, qo‘shimcha savol berasiz va umumiy qiziqishingiz borligini bilib olasiz.

sentences.en: This imaginary example illustrates one of Carnegie's most useful principles: become interested in other people.
sentences.uz: Bu xayoliy misol Karnegining eng foydali tamoyillaridan birini ko‘rsatadi: boshqa odamlarga qiziqing.

sentences.en: You don't need a perfect performance to begin a connection.
sentences.uz: Aloqa o‘rnatish uchun mukammal chiqish shart emas.

sentences.en: You need curiosity that extends beyond waiting for your own turn to speak.
sentences.uz: Sizga shunchaki gapirish navbatingizni kutishdan kengroq bo‘lgan qiziquvchanlik kerak.

sentences.en: Listening takes effort.
sentences.uz: Tinglash kuch talab qiladi.

sentences.en: Put aside distractions.
sentences.uz: Chalg‘ituvchi narsalarni chetga qo‘ying.

sentences.en: Ask about something the person actually cares about.
sentences.uz: Odam chindan qiziqadigan narsa haqida so‘rang.

sentences.en: Follow the answer instead of jumping immediately to your own experience.
sentences.uz: Darhol o‘z tajribangizga o‘tib ketish o‘rniga, javobning davomini kuzating.

sentences.en: Remembering a name or a detail can help, provided it reflects attention rather than a rehearsed technique.
sentences.uz: Ism yoki biror tafsilotni eslab qolish yordam berishi mumkin — faqat bu yodlangan usul emas, chin e’tibor belgisi bo‘lsa.

sentences.en: A second principle is sincere appreciation.
sentences.uz: Ikkinchi tamoyil — samimiy minnatdorlik.

sentences.en: People want their effort to be noticed, but flattery is praise given to obtain something.
sentences.uz: Odamlar mehnati sezilishini xohlaydi, ammo xushomad — nimagadir erishish uchun aytilgan maqtovdir.

sentences.en: Appreciation names something you honestly value.
sentences.uz: Minnatdorlik esa siz chin dildan qadrlaydigan narsani aytib o‘tishdir.

sentences.en: After a teammate improves your presentation, you could say, "The diagram you added made the explanation much clearer. Thank you for spending time on it."
sentences.uz: Jamoadoshingiz taqdimotingizni yaxshilagach, shunday deyishingiz mumkin: «Siz qo‘shgan diagramma tushuntirishni ancha aniqroq qildi. Bunga vaqt ajratganingiz uchun rahmat.»

sentences.en: That gives the person useful information about their contribution.
sentences.uz: Bu odamga uning hissasi haqida foydali ma’lumot beradi.

sentences.en: It also encourages you to look carefully enough to notice what others are doing well.
sentences.uz: Shuningdek, sizni boshqalar nimani yaxshi qilayotganini payqash uchun diqqat bilan qarashga undaydi.

sentences.en: Carnegie also warns against habitual criticism, condemnation, and complaint.
sentences.uz: Karnegi, shuningdek, odat tusiga kirgan tanqid, qoralash va shikoyatdan ogohlantiradi.

sentences.en: Attacking someone's character often makes them defend themselves.
sentences.uz: Kimningdir shaxsiyatiga hujum qilish ko‘pincha uni o‘zini himoya qilishga majbur qiladi.

sentences.en: Consider a teammate who submits work late.
sentences.uz: Ishini kech topshiradigan jamoadoshni olaylik.

sentences.en: Saying, "You're always useless," creates a fight about their identity.
sentences.uz: «Sen doim befoydasan» deyish uning shaxsiyati ustidan janjal chiqaradi.

sentences.en: Saying, "We needed this yesterday, and now we have less time to check it," keeps attention on the problem.
sentences.uz: «Bu bizga kecha kerak edi, endi uni tekshirishga kamroq vaqtimiz qoldi» deyish esa e’tiborni muammoning o‘zida ushlab turadi.

sentences.en: You can then ask what happened and agree on a specific next step.
sentences.uz: Keyin nima bo‘lganini so‘rab, aniq keyingi qadam bo‘yicha kelishib olishingiz mumkin.

sentences.en: Respectful language still allows clear expectations and consequences.
sentences.uz: Hurmatli til aniq talablar va oqibatlarni ham aytishga imkon beradi.

sentences.en: You do not have to pretend that harmful or unreliable behaviour is acceptable.
sentences.uz: Zararli yoki ishonchsiz xatti-harakatni maqbul deb ko‘rsatishingiz shart emas.

sentences.en: Another idea is to consider what the other person wants.
sentences.uz: Yana bir g‘oya — boshqa odam nimani xohlashini o‘ylab ko‘rish.

sentences.en: Suppose you need volunteers for a club event.
sentences.uz: Aytaylik, to‘garak tadbiri uchun ko‘ngillilar kerak.

sentences.en: Explaining only that you're overwhelmed gives them little reason to participate.
sentences.uz: Faqat ishingiz boshingizdan oshib ketganini aytish ularga qatnashish uchun deyarli sabab bermaydi.

sentences.en: Ask what would make the work meaningful for them.
sentences.uz: Bu ish ular uchun nimasi bilan mazmunli bo‘lishi mumkinligini so‘rang.

sentences.en: Someone may want design experience; another may enjoy meeting visitors.
sentences.uz: Kimdir dizayn tajribasini xohlashi mumkin, boshqasiga esa mehmonlar bilan tanishish yoqishi mumkin.

sentences.en: A fair request connects a real need with an honest benefit.
sentences.uz: Adolatli iltimos haqiqiy ehtiyojni halol foyda bilan bog‘laydi.

sentences.en: The same respect matters during disagreement.
sentences.uz: Xuddi shu hurmat kelishmovchilik paytida ham muhim.

sentences.en: Carnegie encourages people to avoid turning discussion into a contest over who can embarrass whom.
sentences.uz: Karnegi muhokamani «kim kimni uyaltiradi» degan bellashuvga aylantirmaslikka chaqiradi.

sentences.en: Before answering, try to explain the other person's concern accurately.
sentences.uz: Javob berishdan oldin suhbatdoshingizning xavotirini aniq ifodalab berishga harakat qiling.

sentences.en: You might discover that you agree about the goal but disagree about the method.
sentences.uz: Balki maqsad bo‘yicha rozi ekaningizni, faqat usulda kelisha olmayotganingizni bilib qolarsiz.

sentences.en: And when you're wrong, admit it.
sentences.uz: Xato qilganingizda esa buni tan oling.

sentences.en: If you misunderstood a message and blamed someone unfairly, explain the mistake plainly.
sentences.uz: Agar xabarni noto‘g‘ri tushunib, kimnidir nohaq ayblagan bo‘lsangiz, xatoingizni ochiq tushuntiring.

sentences.en: Defending an obvious error usually makes the conversation harder.
sentences.uz: Ochiq-oydin xatoni himoya qilish odatda suhbatni qiyinlashtiradi.

sentences.en: Taking responsibility gives you a better starting point for repairing trust.
sentences.uz: Mas’uliyatni bo‘yningizga olish ishonchni tiklash uchun yaxshiroq boshlanish beradi.

sentences.en: When helping someone improve, Carnegie favours preserving dignity: acknowledge real progress, ask questions, and make the next improvement feel achievable.
sentences.uz: Kimgadir yaxshilanishga yordam berayotganda Karnegi uning qadr-qimmatini saqlashni ma’qul ko‘radi: haqiqiy yutuqni e’tirof eting, savol bering va keyingi qadamni erishsa bo‘ladigandek ko‘rsating.

sentences.en: For a nervous presenter, identify one thing that worked, then practise one specific change together.
sentences.uz: Hayajonlangan ma’ruzachiga yaxshi chiqqan bitta jihatni ayting, keyin birgalikda bitta aniq o‘zgarishni mashq qiling.

sentences.en: A manageable next step can be more useful than a list of everything that went badly.
sentences.uz: Uddalasa bo‘ladigan keyingi qadam yomon o‘tgan hamma narsaning ro‘yxatidan foydaliroq bo‘lishi mumkin.

sentences.en: Bookly's caution is to use these ideas with honesty.
sentences.uz: Bookly ogohlantiradi: bu g‘oyalardan halollik bilan foydalaning.

sentences.en: Other people have the right to disagree or decline a request.
sentences.uz: Boshqalar rozi bo‘lmaslik yoki iltimosni rad etish huquqiga ega.

sentences.en: Respect loses its meaning when it becomes a tool for pressuring someone into saying yes.
sentences.uz: Hurmat kimnidir «ha» deyishga majburlash quroliga aylanganda o‘z ma’nosini yo‘qotadi.

sentences.en: Here's today's challenge.
sentences.uz: Mana bugungi topshiriq.

sentences.en: In your next conversation, ask one thoughtful question and listen to the whole answer.
sentences.uz: Keyingi suhbatingizda bitta o‘ylangan savol bering va javobni oxirigacha tinglang.

sentences.en: Then offer one specific appreciation, if you honestly have one.
sentences.uz: So‘ng, agar chin dildan aytadigan gapingiz bo‘lsa, bitta aniq minnatdorlik bildiring.

sentences.en: Notice what changes when the other person has room to be heard.
sentences.uz: Suhbatdoshingizga tinglanish uchun imkon berilganda nima o‘zgarishiga e’tibor bering.

vocab.definition: showing that you value someone or something
vocab.example: A short note of appreciation can make someone's day.
vocab.exampleUz: Qisqa minnatdorlik so‘zi kimningdir kunini yaxshilashi mumkin.

vocab.definition: praise that is not sincere, given to get something
vocab.example: People can usually tell flattery from honest praise.
vocab.exampleUz: Odamlar odatda xushomadni samimiy maqtovdan ajrata oladi.

vocab.definition: the respect that every person deserves
vocab.example: Correct mistakes without hurting someone's dignity.

vocab.definition: saying what is wrong with someone or something
vocab.example: Useful criticism focuses on the problem, not the person.
vocab.exampleUz: Foydali tanqid insonga emas, muammoga qaratiladi.

vocab.definition: the wish to learn or know more
a situation where people have different opinions
vocab.example: We had a disagreement, but we stayed respectful.
vocab.exampleUz: Oramizda kelishmovchilik bo‘ldi, lekin hurmatni saqladik.

vocab.definition: to say that something is true, often a mistake
vocab.example: It is brave to admit you were wrong.

questions.prompt: In the club example, what helped you connect with the other member?
questions.promptUz: To‘garak misolida boshqa a’zo bilan yaqinlashishga nima yordam berdi?
options: Asking about her work and listening to the answer
optionsUz: Uning ishi haqida so‘rash va javobini tinglash
questions.explanationUz: Karnegining tamoyili: boshqa odamlarga chin dildan qiziqing — savol bering va tinglang.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between flattery and appreciation?
questions.promptUz: Xushomad va minnatdorlik o‘rtasidagi farq nima?
options: Flattery is praise given to get something; appreciation names something you honestly value
Appreciation is always longer than flattery
optionsUz: Xushomad — nimagadir erishish uchun maqtov; minnatdorlik — chin dildan qadrlaganingizni aytish
questions.explanationUz: Minnatdorlik aniq va samimiy bo‘ladi: masalan, «Siz qo‘shgan diagramma tushuntirishni ancha aniqroq qildi».

questions.prompt: How should you respond to a teammate who submits work late?
questions.promptUz: Ishini kech topshirgan jamoadoshga qanday javob berish kerak?
options: Tell them they are always useless
Focus on the problem, ask what happened and agree on a next step
optionsUz: Muammoga e’tibor qaratish, nima bo‘lganini so‘rash va keyingi qadamga kelishish
questions.explanationUz: Hurmatli til ham aniq talablarni aytishga imkon beradi — shaxsga emas, muammoga e’tibor qarating.

takeaway.en: In your next conversation, ask one thoughtful question, listen to the whole answer, and offer one specific appreciation if you honestly have one.
takeaway.uz: Keyingi suhbatingizda bitta o‘ylangan savol bering, javobni oxirigacha tinglang va chin dildan aytadigan gapingiz bo‘lsa, bitta aniq minnatdorlik bildiring.
